messages:
Sam: Quick heads-up — started canary bringup for reranker-v3 quant (q4f). Noticed a small but consistent MRR dip on short queries (2-6 tokens). Anyone on call?
Maria: I saw the alert earlier, thanks. Do you have the bench numbers vs fp16 baseline?
Sam: Pasting quick slice: fp16 baseline (short queries): NDCG@10=0.412, MRR@10=0.278. q4f canary: NDCG@10=0.407, MRR@10=0.248. Drop concentrated on tail of short queries.
Lee: Hmm 0.03 MRR absolute is pretty visible. Did we preserve tokenizer & padding exactly? Short queries are sensitive.
Sam: Good point. Candidate ordering and tokenization parity were supposed to be identical, but the build used a new tokenizer wheel (tokenizer v2.1). Will re-run with tokenizer pinned to v2.0.
Anita: Also check KV cache behavior — quant runtime had a small change to kv eviction order in next patch. If cache prefixing differs, reranker sees different context distribution.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started at 2025-05-12T10:03:53Z for host pool canary-rlk-2.
Maria: Can you run an isolated eval that mirrors production candidate ordering? Our offline bench sometimes shuffles top-k differently. Use the exact candidate pipeline: dedupe -> score -> rank.
Sam: Running targeted eval now. Command I used:
```
run_eval \
  --model reranker_v3_q4f \
  --baseline reranker_v3_fp16 \
  --cohort short_queries \
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 \
  --samples 12k \
  --preserve-order true \
  --tokenizer v2.0
```
Lee: Also try disabling batching and kvpack to rule out micro-batching interactions. Short queries can be starved by batching heuristics.
Anita: And re-run with candidate text normalized the same way — our new ingest pipeline strips punctuation differently (lowering signal for 1-2 token queries).
Maria: If the regression persists after tokenizer/candidate-order parity, we should run a small A/B in canary with fp16 fallback policy enabled (keep traffic split 90/10). See rollout config: `rollout:canary -> fallback:reranker_v3_fp16`
Sam: Eval results (prelim): q4f with tokenizer v2.0 + preserve-order + batching=off -> NDCG@10=0.411, MRR@10=0.275. So tokenizer/preserve-order accounts for most of it.
Lee: Good. Suggest we add a unit test in eval harness to assert tokenizer parity and candidate-order parity for bringups.
Anita: Agree. I'll open a quick PR to pin tokenizer in the deployment manifest and add a harness check.
Maria: Also let's add a small golden set of 500 short queries to the quality monitor for reranker-v3 so future quant changes trigger regression alerts. Thresholds: MRR drop > 0.01 or NDCG drop > 0.005 for that slice.
Sam: Action items: (1) Anita pins tokenizer & PR for harness check. (2) I will re-run full canary with pinned tokenizer and enable fp16 fallback. (3) Maria will add the short-query golden set to monitor with threshold.
Anita: I'll send PR link shortly.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary updated at 2025-05-12T11:02:13Z (reranker-v3 pinned-tokenizer). Rollout still in 10% canary.
Sam: Thanks — results look good so far. If no further regressions in 2h we'll promote.
Maria: Nice triage everyone :thumbsup:
Lee: Small but useful reminder — short-query cohorts are brittle under any infra change. Good catch.
Sam: Closing the loop later with a short postmortem note in ops channel if anything interesting pops up.
